Subject: Strato Systems — 3yr price lock request

Kim — quick one for Deal Desk / exec review. Strato (Emma Li) has asked for a binding 3-year price lock on their committed capacity. Details: 3-year committed contract, $2.45M ARR year 1, with modest growth in usage. The ask: guaranteed list price hold for 36 months, uplift cap of 4% year-over-year, and a renewal protection clause that prevents >5% price increases on renewal without a 120-day notice and mutual agreement.

Why escalation: this is outside standard guardrails for multi-year pricing (we typically allow 2-year locks and uplift caps up to 6% with finance sign-off). If we give a 3-year lock with a 4% cap it materially reduces upside and increases risk on cost inflation. Customer has leverage: they're buying a Reserved Dedicated pool and want the stability to move prod traffic.

Attachments: Price_Model_Scenario.xlsx (sensitivity to uplift rates).

Request: need exec guidance and approval (or alternate language) to respond to Emma by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Options I think worth considering:
- Approve as requested if legal signs a limited-scope clause (price lock applies to the specific SKU list in the SOW only).

- Decline and offer a 24-month lock with 4% cap and an option to extend at mutually agreed rates.

Need: explicit go/no-go and any required guardrails we should include in the amendment language. Please respond with a decision and any redlines within 48 hours — customer is pushing for a written commitment.

Kim — quick read through the model. Attaching an exec financial memo with NPV impact at 3%, 4%, and 6% uplift scenarios. My take:

- Approve a 3-year lock if we (a) limit the lock to the agreed capacity profile (SKU-level), and (b) add a material cost-pass-through clause for identifiable infra cost increases beyond our control (e.g., public cloud pricing spikes > X%).
- The 4% uplift cap is tight; from a finance POV 5% is the safer floor. If we accept 4% I'd ask for an early termination fee if usage falls below 70% of committed base in any year.

If leadership wants to keep competitive posture, we can accept 4% but require: SKU list, usage floors, and a 120-day notice for renewal pricing — otherwise renewal defaults to our published committed pricing at that time.

I can sign off subject to legal drafting the clause and finance confirming the required IRR thresholds.

- Contract term: 36 months.
